chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: The Newark Charter Company buses that New York bands rented
summary: Most New York bands used Newark Charter Company's cheap per-mile buses with instruments at the back and bags on top; Fletcher and Horace never owned one.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Uh-huh. At that time did you have buses that were especially built or at least furnished for this kind of traveling, or was it just renting a (unintelligible) regular, like a Greyhound bus or something?

No, I tell you, there was a certain bus company that most of the bands that traveled out of New York City used. It was called the Newark Charter Company, and I think the reason for that is because their rate by the mile was so much lower than the Greyhound or the Santa Fe, one of those things, and all the booking agents and the promoters got so that they knew this particular company, and they really gave them a lot of work. And, man, they had plenty of buses; they had, oh, 75 or 100 buses, Newark Charter Company, and they weren't fixed up any different from any other bus, except now I realize they didn't have as soft of seats as the Greyhound, but I guess this is one of the reasons why the mileage that they charged was far less than the Greyhound or

some of the other companies.

But nevertheless, you know, they piled the musicians in there, and they were doing -- put all the instruments in the back of the bus, all back of that last seat, you know, and a lot of things, like the boys', their bags and things would go up on top of the bus, you know, and they'd have a canopy on top, naturally. And mechanically, though, so that you never heard of many breakdowns. The buses always got you there.

One thing for sure, by using the bus, you know that you had your group there all the time and together. If you broke down, you broke down together, you know. Which didn't happen too often.
Did either you or Fletcher ever own a bus?
No, we never owned a bus. We actually did own it by how much we paid.
